# Lumen Labs - Company Context Index

> **This is fictional demo data for Lumen Labs, a made-up B2B SaaS startup. It is read-only and shared across all users. Do not edit it, and never present it as real company data. "Today" in this dataset is 2026-10-12; data runs through 30 Sep 2026 with October partial.**

Lumen Labs sells Lumen Insights (customer-feedback analytics). 40 employees, $80,000 MRR, 28 customers, $6.02M cash, ~20 months runway. Customers are keyed by `customer_id` (CUST-xxxx) and employees by `employee_id` (Exxx) in every file.

## Start here, by bot
| Bot | Questions | Read first |
|---|---|---|
| CFO / Finance | MRR, ARR, churn, cash, runway, burn, budget vs actual, failed payments | `finance/summary.md`, `finance/stripe-export/mrr-by-month.csv`, `failed-payments.csv`, `customers.csv` |
| HR | headcount, org, comp bands, leave, open roles, candidates, policies, onboarding | `hr/bamboohr-export/employees.csv`, `hr/salary-bands.md`, `hr/open-roles.md`, `hr/greenhouse-export/candidates.csv`, `hr/policies/*` |
| Sales | pipeline, forecast, deal status, pricing/discount rules, objections | `sales/hubspot-export/deals.csv`, `sales/q4-forecast.md`, `sales/sales-playbook.md` |
| Customer Success | account health, renewals, escalations, churn reasons | `customer-success/account-health.csv`, `zendesk-export/tickets.csv`, `churn-log.md` |
| Marketing | campaign ROI, signups by channel, positioning, Q4 plan | `marketing/campaigns.csv`, `signups-by-channel.csv`, `brand-and-positioning.md`, `content-calendar-q4.md` |
| Legal | contract renewals, notice deadlines, liability, templates, compliance | `legal/contracts-register.csv`, `legal/compliance-status.md`, `msa-template.md`, `nda-template.md` |
| Assistant / Orchestrator | company background, priorities, cross-functional questions | `company/overview.md`, then the relevant function above |

Cross-functional questions (e.g. "what is the status of Northwind Logistics?") need: Stripe `customers.csv` + `failed-payments.csv`, `account-health.csv`, Zendesk `tickets.csv`, HubSpot `deals.csv` and `contracts-register.csv`, joined by `customer_id`.

## File map
### company/
- `company/overview.md` - what Lumen does, pricing tiers, ICP, founders, funding, org summary, metrics snapshot, Q4 2026 OKRs (all bots)

### finance/ (CFO)
- `finance/stripe-export/mrr-by-month.csv` - Oct 2024-Sep 2026: beginning, new, expansion, contraction, churned, ending MRR, customer counts
- `finance/stripe-export/customers.csv` - every customer ever (28 active, 9 churned): plan, seats, MRR, status, country
- `finance/stripe-export/failed-payments.csv` - failed invoice payments, status and retry dates
- `finance/summary.md` - cash, burn, runway, 6-month P&L, Q3 budget vs actual, collections watch

### hr/ (HR)
- `hr/bamboohr-export/employees.csv` - all 40 employees: title, dept, manager, location, start date, band, salary (USD), leave balance
- `hr/salary-bands.md` - bands L1-L6 with USD ranges and comp rules
- `hr/open-roles.md` - 4 open roles with rationale and pipeline counts
- `hr/greenhouse-export/candidates.csv` - 19 candidates, stages, interviewers
- `hr/policies/employee-handbook.md`, `leave-policy.md`, `remote-work-policy.md` - policies
- `hr/onboarding-checklist.md` - new-hire checklist

### sales/ (Sales)
- `sales/hubspot-export/deals.csv` - 28 deals (open, closed won, closed lost) with ARR, owner, notes
- `sales/sales-playbook.md` - ICP, personas, discovery, objections, discount rules
- `sales/q4-forecast.md` - Q4 bookings forecast, renewals due, scenarios

### customer-success/ (Customer Success)
- `customer-success/account-health.csv` - health score, usage trend, NPS, CSM, renewal date, risk flag for 28 active + 3 Q3 churned accounts
- `customer-success/zendesk-export/tickets.csv` - 36 recent tickets, including open P1 escalations
- `customer-success/churn-log.md` - 2026 churned accounts and reasons

### marketing/ (Marketing)
- `marketing/campaigns.csv` - Q2-Q3 actuals and Q4 budgets: spend, leads, MQLs, SQLs, pipeline
- `marketing/signups-by-channel.csv` - monthly trial signups by channel, Oct 2025-Sep 2026
- `marketing/brand-and-positioning.md` - positioning, pillars, tone, competitors
- `marketing/content-calendar-q4.md` - Q4 plan incl. SSO and Enterprise Readiness launch

### legal/ (Legal)
- `legal/contracts-register.csv` - key customer and vendor contracts: renewal, auto-renew, notice period and deadline, liability cap, SLA
- `legal/msa-template.md`, `legal/nda-template.md` - templates
- `legal/compliance-status.md` - SOC 2 Type II progress, GDPR, India DPDP, HIPAA, open items

## The story in the data (for demo cross-checks)
Q3 2026 churn rose ($8,100 MRR): Redwood Commerce (no SSO), Stratus Cloudworks (Aug 14 outage), Vantage Mobility (champion left). Northwind Logistics (CUST-1021, $7,200 MRR, largest account) is Critical: failed payment, 2 open P1s, low health, renewal 2026-12-15 with a notice deadline of 2026-10-16. Open roles (Senior SRE, CSM) respond to it, and a Q4 SSO/enterprise launch is planned in marketing.

# Finance Summary - Lumen Labs (as of 2026-09-30)

_Fictional demo data. Source of truth for figures: `stripe-export/*.csv` (revenue) and this file (cash, P&L, budget). All amounts USD. Revenue recognised is approximated as month-end MRR._

## Position at 30 Sep 2026
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Cash in bank | $6,019,000 |
| Average monthly net burn (Q3 2026) | $295,061 |
| Runway (cash / avg Q3 net burn) | 20.4 months |
| Ending MRR (Sep 2026) | $80,000 (ARR $960,000) |
| Active paying customers | 28 (ARPA $2,857/mo) |
| Series A | $8.0M closed June 2025 (led by a fictional fund, Foundry Peak Ventures); seed $1.5M in 2022 |
| Net revenue retention (TTM) | 97.9% |
| Gross revenue retention (TTM) | 87.4% |
| Q3 churned MRR | $8,100 (Q2: $800) - Redwood Commerce, Stratus Cloudworks, Vantage Mobility |

Burn arithmetic: net burn = cloud COGS + payroll + software + marketing programs + other opex - revenue. Runway = cash / net burn. Payroll is base salary from `hr/bamboohr-export/employees.csv` x 1.15 (benefits, employer taxes), by month of hire; annual base payroll today is $3,050,000 for 40 employees.

## P&L, last 6 months
| Line | 2026-04 | 2026-05 | 2026-06 | 2026-07 | 2026-08 | 2026-09 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (month-end MRR) | $81,700 | $82,900 | $83,900 | $82,900 | $82,200 | $80,000 |
| Cloud infrastructure (COGS) | -$19,200 | -$19,800 | -$20,500 | -$21,300 | -$26,900 | -$24,100 |
| Gross profit | $62,500 | $63,100 | $63,400 | $61,600 | $55,300 | $55,900 |
| Payroll (loaded) | -$273,508 | -$280,217 | -$282,133 | -$289,800 | -$292,292 | -$292,292 |
| Software & tools | -$12,800 | -$12,900 | -$13,100 | -$13,400 | -$13,600 | -$13,600 |
| Marketing programs | -$18,766 | -$18,766 | -$18,768 | -$21,666 | -$21,666 | -$21,668 |
| Other opex (rent, legal, audit, recruiting) | -$24,000 | -$24,200 | -$24,500 | -$25,000 | -$26,500 | -$26,500 |
| Operating result | -$266,574 | -$272,983 | -$275,101 | -$288,266 | -$298,758 | -$298,160 |
| Net burn (positive = cash out) | $266,574 | $272,983 | $275,101 | $288,266 | $298,758 | $298,160 |
| Cash at month end | $7,452,268 | $7,179,285 | $6,904,184 | $6,615,918 | $6,317,160 | $6,019,000 |
| Gross margin % | 76.5% | 76.1% | 75.6% | 74.3% | 67.3% | 69.9% |

Notes: August cloud cost includes emergency capacity and Datadog expansion after the 2026-08-14 ingestion outage. Marketing programs equal the quarterly totals in `marketing/campaigns.csv` (Q2 $56,300, Q3 $65,000) split evenly by month.

## Budget vs actual, Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep)
| Line | Budget | Actual | Variance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $259,800 | $245,100 | -$14,700 unfav |
| Cloud infrastructure | $65,100 | $72,300 | -$7,200 unfav |
| Payroll (loaded) | $900,600 | $874,384 | +$26,216 fav |
| Software & tools | $41,400 | $40,600 | +$800 fav |
| Marketing programs | $65,000 | $65,000 | +$0 fav |
| Other opex | $74,900 | $78,000 | -$3,100 unfav |
| Net burn | $887,200 | $885,184 | +$2,016 fav |

Commentary: revenue missed budget because three mid-market accounts churned in Q3 ($8,100 MRR) while new logos landed late in the quarter. Payroll is under budget as the Senior SRE, CSM and Identity/SSO engineer roles are still open (see `hr/open-roles.md`); cloud ran over budget because of the August incident (emergency capacity and Datadog expansion). Net burn is $885,184 for the quarter vs budget $887,200.

## Receivables and collections watch
- Northwind Logistics: Oct invoice $7,200 failed 4 times (see `stripe-export/failed-payments.csv`, FP-2001), plus a pending SLA credit request (customer asks ~$2,160, finance calc $720). Exposure: $7,200 now, $86,400 ARR at renewal 2026-12-15.
- Drift Media: $500 failed 2026-10-01 (expired card); retry 2026-10-13.
- All other Q3 failures were recovered within 14 days.

## Tracking
- Cash zero date at current burn: about June 2028.
- Fundraising plan: start Series B conversations at ~12 months runway; target ARR milestone $1.5M.

import glob, json, os, re, sys

os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
log = open("server3001.log").read()
by_agent = {}
for m in re.finditer(r"TEMP-MEASURE (\{.*\})", log):
    d = json.loads(m.group(1))
    by_agent[d["traceId"]] = d["byAgent"]

# Key facts from company/lumen-labs (finance/summary.md, tickets ZD-10431, contracts-register CT-C-001,
# failed-payments FP-2001, account-health, q4-forecast).
CHECKS = {
    "$720 formula (10%)": r"\$720",
    "$2,160 ask (30%)": r"\$2,160",
    "$1,440 delta": r"\$1,440",
    "$7,200 MRR": r"\$7,200",
    "$86,400 ARR": r"\$86,400",
    "cash $6.02M": r"\$6,019,000|\$6\.02\s?M",
    "burn $295,061": r"\$295,061|\$295k|\$295,1",
    "runway 20.4 mo": r"20\.4",
    "post-churn runway ~19.9": r"19\.9",
    "deadline 16 Oct": r"16 Oct|2026-10-16|Oct 16|October 16",
    "renewal 15 Dec": r"15 Dec|2026-12-15|Dec 15|December 15",
    "9.0% of ARR": r"9\.0\s?%|9%",
}

rows = []
for label in sys.argv[1:]:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"stream-{label}-*.json")):
        i = f.rsplit("-", 1)[1].split(".")[0]
        parts = json.load(open(f))
        out = open(f"out-{label}-{i}.txt").read()
        latency = float(re.search(r"^--- ([\d.]+)s", out, re.M).group(1))
        usage = [p for p in parts if p["type"] == "data-turn-usage"][-1]["data"]
        text = "".join(p.get("delta", "") for p in parts if p["type"] == "text-delta")
        calls = {}
        for p in parts:
            if p["type"] == "tool-input-available":
                calls[p["toolCallId"]] = {"name": p["toolName"]}
            if p["type"] == "tool-output-available" and p["toolCallId"] in calls:
                calls[p["toolCallId"]]["out"] = p["output"]
        primary_reads = [c for c in calls.values() if c["name"] == "company_read_file"]
        cfo_files, cfo_bytes, cfo_text = [], 0, 0
        for c in calls.values():
            if c["name"] == "agent-cfoAgent" and isinstance(c.get("out"), dict):
                cfo_text += len(c["out"].get("text", ""))
                for r in c["out"].get("subAgentToolResults", []):
                    if r.get("toolName") == "company_read_file":
                        cfo_files.append((r.get("args") or {}).get("path"))
                        cfo_bytes += len(json.dumps(r.get("result")))
        specialists = sorted({c["name"][6:] for c in calls.values() if c["name"].startswith("agent-")})
        missing = [k for k, rx in CHECKS.items() if not re.search(rx, text)]
        rows.append(
            dict(
                run=f"{label}-{i}", cost=usage["costUsd"], tokens=usage["tokens"], out_tokens=usage["outputTokens"],
                steps=usage["steps"], capped=usage["capped"], reason=usage["reason"], latency=latency,
                primary_reads=len(primary_reads), cfo_reads=len(cfo_files), cfo_kb=round(cfo_bytes / 1000, 1), cfo_text=cfo_text,
                specialists=specialists, trace=usage["traceId"], by_agent=by_agent.get(usage["traceId"]), missing=missing,
                answer_chars=len(text),
            )
        )
for r in rows:
    print(json.dumps(r))

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.content:
## Usage caps

Every chat turn (one user message, or one approval resume, and everything the agent does to answer it: all model steps, tool calls and delegated sub-agent calls) is limited per user and per agent by a **cost cap** (default $0.25) and a **token cap** (default 300,000 tokens). Each user sets their own caps per agent; they are stored in `data/auth.db` (`agent_caps`) and persist across sessions and restarts. The caps of the agent being chatted with apply, including to the sub-agents it delegates to.

- `GET /api/agents/:agentId/caps` returns `{ costCapUsd, tokenCap, defaults }`; `PUT` with `{ costCapUsd, tokenCap }` saves them (both must be greater than 0; at most 1000 USD and 100,000,000 tokens); `DELETE` resets to the defaults. Signed-in users only, own caps only.
- Cost is estimated from `src/usage/pricing.ts` (DeepSeek's published peak prices; input tokens the provider reports as cache hits, `usage.cachedInputTokens`, are priced at the cache-hit rate and the rest at the cache-miss rate, and a step that reports no cached count is priced entirely at the cache-miss rate; unknown models use a high fallback price).
- A processor on every agent (`src/usage/turn-budget.ts`) adds up each model step's usage. Once a cap is exceeded the run stops before the next model call (tools the last step requested still run); the partial reply is kept and a closing note explains which limit was hit.
- The chat stream carries a `data-turn-usage` part (`{ costUsd, tokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens, steps, capCostUsd, capTokens, capped, reason, final }`) after each model step and once more at the end. The final usage (plus the turn's Neatlogs `traceId`) is also on the finish part and on the saved reply as `metadata.turnUsage`. Neatlogs traces get `app.turn_cost_usd`, `app.turn_tokens`, `app.turn_steps` and `app.turn_capped`, plus a `cost-capped` or `token-capped` tag.
- After a turn, Neatlogs' own numbers are shown next to the estimate under the bot pill (e.g. "Est. $0.0022 · 7.3k" / "Neatlogs $0.0001 · 7.3k tokens"). Once the reply is sent and the trace has ended, the server flushes the Neatlogs exporter and polls `get_trace_context` for that trace (server-side, through the shared Neatlogs MCP client; never exposed to an agent) until it is finalized, for up to ~45 s (`src/usage/neatlogs-usage.ts`). In practice it is ready about 4-6 s after the reply. The result is saved on the reply as `metadata.neatlogsUsage` (`{ status: "pending" | "ready" | "unavailable", traceId, costUsd, tokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, checkedAt, fetchedAt }`), so a reload shows it. The browser polls `GET /api/chat/:agentId/messages/:messageId/neatlogs-usage`, which only finds replies in the caller's own chat (404 otherwise) and, when no poll is running and the last check is over 10 s old, checks Neatlogs once more. Neatlogs' cost is usually lower than the estimate because it counts DeepSeek cache hits; the caps still use the estimate.
- The Neatlogs line links to the turn's trace in the Neatlogs dashboard (new tab). The link template comes from `GET /api/neatlogs/trace-link`: `NEATLOGS_TRACE_URL` (containing `{traceId}`) if set, otherwise built from the org and project ids that Neatlogs' `whoami` reports for `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`; without either, the line is plain text.

## Key Integrations

- **NeatLogs**: All Mastra agents are wrapped with `neatlogs/mastra`, recording agent runs, model steps, tool calls, inputs/outputs, timing, token usage when returned, and errors. CLI runs have request traces. Tracing does not trim model context.
- **GitHub MCP**: The GitHub Bot uses GitHub's hosted MCP server (`https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`) through `@mastra/mcp`, limited to the context, repos, issues, pull_requests and actions toolsets.
- **Neatlogs MCP**: The Neat Bot uses Neatlogs' hosted MCP server (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`) through `@mastra/mcp`, authenticated with the existing `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. Tools are gated by name (the server sends no read-only annotations): reads run directly, writes and unknown tools need approval.
- **Entire**: Coding-context hooks and checkpoint settings are configured.

## View Neatlogs traces

Set `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in `.env` to your Neatlogs project ingest key, then restart `npm run serve` (or run `npm start -- "Say hello in one sentence"`). Optional `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` selects the ingest endpoint; `NEATLOGS_DEBUG=true` enables SDK diagnostics. Without a key, dashboard export is disabled and startup prints a warning.

Open https://app.neatlogs.com and select the project matching your key. Open its traces view and find the `cli.request` run. The terminal prints the exact `traceId` for each request; use it to identify the run. Expand the agent/model/tool spans to inspect each step. Agent/model/tool tracing captures conversation content and tool results.

`npx neatlogs doctor --local --json` validates the local SDK pipeline without credentials or network calls. `node --env-file=.env node_modules/neatlogs/dist/cli.mjs doctor --probe --json` sends generated diagnostic spans to your configured project and checks their persisted trace. It does not call an LLM. CLI requests explicitly flush at shutdown; the long-running server uses SDK batching and signal shutdown handlers.

## Credits
